overview: This 394-page file combines Board of Economic Warfare records and original and corrected assessments of Japan’s 1943 war economy with U.S. Embassy despatches from Chungking. Most later pages translate intercepted Japanese commercial messages detailing trade, shipping, supplies, and finance across occupied East and Southeast Asia. It also includes reports on oil-facility demolition in the Netherlands East Indies and North Borneo.
interest: The corrected economic assessment and dated commercial intercepts let historians compare U.S. strategic judgments with detailed evidence of Japanese trade.
